summary: Complete BUG-0203 in the ISO library UI: failed and needs-attention imports offer a confirmed discard action that uses existing DELETE /api/v1/media/{id}, reconciles a lost response from GET /api/v1/media, and reloads the list. Queued, dispatched and succeeded rows offer no discard action; retry remains POST /api/v1/media/download with a new request_id. API impact: existing contract.

guide.reason: The guide now names the confirmed ISO-library action, its eligible failed and needs-attention states, and the retained audit history.

api.reason: API impact: existing contract. The UI calls implemented DELETE and GET /api/v1/media and retains POST /api/v1/media/download for retry; neither request, response, authorization rule nor Core command changes.

roadmap.reason: Completes the UI half of an existing defect fix without changing milestone status.

state.reason: Discard removes the disposable Controller import row and staging bytes for an import that did not become host media. Its task and audit history remain; the UI stores no new pool or media state.
state.record: Controller operation and audit history retain the discard and failed import; its disposable staging/import row is removed. Successful ISO files and identities remain in the Core managed journal and repository media directory, recovered by a fresh Controller from Inventory.managed.media.

verification.method: npm --prefix web run test, npm --prefix web run typecheck, npm --prefix web run build, python3 scripts/check_docs.py --worktree, and python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_repository_privacy.py'. The focused UI check renders eligible and ineligible rows and asserts confirmation, GET reconciliation after a DELETE failure, reload and the existing retry route. Chromium against deployed Controller/Core then discarded a disposable HTTPS-downgrade failure, removed its row and retained task history; a browser-uploaded disposable 64 MiB ISO reached the live host-ready banner.
